title: Intention-driven database search integration
summary: Natural-language database meaning is represented as structured plans, assessed against schema/runtime evidence, and executed through an injected backend. Dev30 consumes database-declared capabilities before compatibility probes.
invariants: Intention Service owns conversation state, plan transformation, ambiguity and dispatch readiness.
Schema owns tables, columns, keys and valid traversal edges; semantic hints add business meaning; synonyms add wording only.
Meaning and executability are distinct; feasibility depends on current evidence.
Execution path is independent of semantic meaning and may switch without reparsing the intention.
Database capability evidence must prefer a public provider/version feature registry when available; executable probes are fallback only.
Application/profile code receives a common executor from one composition root.
Independent regression scenarios use fresh IntentionService sessions; genuine multi-turn tests share history.
Blind qualification may only use names/fields/values discovered earlier in that same session.
